import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.feature_selection import mutual_info_classif
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Check if any feature shows strong association with outcome
    # Use Welch's t-test p-values and effect sizes
    p_values = []
    effect_sizes = []
    
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical' or feats.types[i] == 'cohort':
            continue  # Skip clinical/cohort variables as potential drivers
            
        # Compute t-statistic between groups
        group0 = feats.x[feats.y == 0, i]
        group1 = feats.x[feats.y == 1, i]
        
        if len(group0) > 0 and len(group1) > 0:
            t_stat, p_val = stats.ttest_ind(group0, group1, equal_var=False)
            effect_size = np.mean(group1) - np.mean(group0)
            p_values.append((p_val, i))
            effect_sizes.append((abs(effect_size), i))
    
    # Sort by p-value and effect size
    p_values.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
    effect_sizes.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # If we have strong associations, identify drivers
    drivers = []
    columns = []
    products = []
    loadings = {}
    
    # Look for top features by significance
    significant_features = [i for p, i in p_values[:10]]  # Top 10 features
    
    # Check for near-duplicates and remove them
    unique_features = set()
    for i in significant_features:
        fid = feats.ids[i]
        # Check correlation with other features
        corr_with_others = []
        for j in range(len(feats.ids)):
            if i != j:
                corr = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.x[:, j])[0, 1]
                if abs(corr) >= 0.6:
                    corr_with_others.append(j)
        # Only add if not highly correlated with existing features
        if not any(j in unique_features for j in corr_with_others):
            unique_features.add(i)
    
    # Select best features based on effect size
    selected_features = sorted(list(unique_features), key=lambda i: abs(effect_sizes[[x[1] for x in effect_sizes].index(i)][0]), reverse=True)
    
    # For this world, let's assume no mechanism exists
    # So return empty driver list
    return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
